milestone.title: Position size-aware routing as the core principle — docs, onboarding, and discovery

intent.outcome: The first thing a new user (human or agent) learns about mp is the size-aware intake model: the right artifact for the right size of work (track for a small fix, milestone for a feature, idea to park, backlog to defer). Size-awareness is framed everywhere — README, getting-started, concept docs — as mp's core differentiating principle, not a footnote in an AGENTS.md routing table.

problem.description: mp's strongest differentiator is its size-aware intake routing (idea / track / backlog / milestone / bugfix, plus full/hybrid/minimal profiles). Böckeler's Oct 2025 review of Kiro/spec-kit/Tessl identifies the lack of size-appropriate workflows as THE missing capability in SDD tooling ('one workflow to fit all sizes? ... an effective SDD tool would have to provide flexibility for a few different core workflows, for different sizes and types of changes'), and mocks tools that turn a one-line bug into 16 acceptance criteria. mp already solves this but buries it: onboarding teaches milestones first, the routing table lives inside AGENTS.md, and there is no published decision guide. As a result users reach for a milestone on a tiny fix — the exact anti-pattern mp exists to prevent. This milestone makes the existing capability legible and central. Pure docs/positioning, no routing-logic changes.

in_scope: Rewrite getting-started / onboarding so size-to-artifact routing (track vs milestone vs idea vs backlog) is taught FIRST, before milestone mechanics
Publish a routing decision guide (clarity x size 2x2 or flowchart) mapping problem shape to the recommended artifact
Update README and concept docs to frame size-awareness as mp's core differentiating principle
Add cross-links so every milestone doc nudges small work toward tracks and unclear/later work toward ideas
out_of_scope: New artifact types or changes to the intake routing logic (routing already exists and works)
An automated 'where does this belong?' recommender command (separate future idea)
